families.source: UKHSA HCAI operational guidance and standards
families.topic: operational management and standards for healthcare-associated infection incidents
families.page_title: Healthcare associated infection (HCAI): operational guidance and standards
evidence_points: The publication provides operational guidance and standards for health protection management of HCAI.
It supports consistent assessment, investigation, response and communication.
The guidance is intended for relevant health protection and healthcare professionals.
The publication is maintained on GOV.UK as an official HCAI resource.
The source is an official GOV.UK primary guidance page managed by UKHSA.
The page was live-opened successfully on 31 July 2026.
Operational guidance must be matched to the organism, setting and current incident evidence.
Standards require local capability, governance and documented implementation.
An incident notification alone does not establish outbreak status or causation.
Final decisions require case definitions, epidemiology, microbiology, setting, controls, communications, responsibilities and review evidence.

families.source: UKHSA mandatory HCAI surveillance data quality statement
families.topic: quality assurance for mandatory healthcare-associated infection surveillance data
families.page_title: Mandatory healthcare associated infection surveillance: data quality statement
evidence_points: The publication describes quality assurance for mandatory HCAI surveillance data.
It covers surveillance of MRSA, MSSA, Gram-negative bacteraemia and C. difficile infection.
The documents explain collection, validation, production and publication controls.
The page provides period-specific data quality statements.
The source is an official GOV.UK primary quality publication managed by UKHSA.
The page was live-opened successfully on 31 July 2026.
Quality statements must be matched to the relevant reporting period and dataset.
Validation controls reduce but do not eliminate missing, late or incorrectly classified records.
A published quality statement does not prove that each individual record is correct.
Final decisions require dataset version, period, completeness, validation, revisions, definitions, exclusions and governance evidence.

families.topic: official statistics for mandatory healthcare-associated infection surveillance
evidence_points: The collection provides official HCAI statistics and links to monthly and annual surveillance outputs.
It includes counts and rates for MRSA, MSSA, E. coli, Pseudomonas, Klebsiella and C. difficile.
The collection links current data releases and dashboard presentations.
The page is maintained by UKHSA.
The source is an official GOV.UK primary statistics collection managed by UKHSA.
The page was live-opened successfully on 31 July 2026.
Statistics require the correct release period, geography, denominator and revision status.
Counts and rates across organisms are not directly interchangeable.
A national rate does not determine an individual provider's cause or preventability.
Final decisions require release version, organism, case definition, denominator, geography, revisions, uncertainty and local comparison evidence.

families.source: UKHSA HCAI quality and methodology information
families.topic: quality and methodology for healthcare-associated infection statistical reports
families.page_title: Quality and methodology information (QMI) for healthcare-associated infections (HCAI) reports
evidence_points: The page explains quality and methodology for UKHSA HCAI statistical reports.
It identifies mandatory surveillance and HCAI data capture systems as principal sources.
The methodology describes comparisons and quality assurance using other surveillance systems.
The page was published or updated in 2026.
The source is an official GOV.UK primary statistics methodology page managed by UKHSA.
The page was live-opened successfully on 31 July 2026.
Methodology should be applied to the specific statistical release and organism.
Cross-system comparisons can reveal discrepancies but do not remove all ascertainment bias.
A statistical designation does not make every estimate suitable for every local decision.
Final decisions require data source, period, definitions, validation, revisions, denominator, uncertainty and intended-use evidence.
